title: Closed complementary subtopoi: factorization and supported module sheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a Grothendieck topos (sheaves of sets on a small site in [def-weil-size-convention]), let $U\hookrightarrow1_{\mathcal T}$ be a subterminal object (a monomorphism to the terminal object), and let $j:\mathcal T/U\to\mathcal T$ be its open slice topos. The full subcategory of objects $H$ for which $U\times H\to U$ is an isomorphism is a topos $\mathcal Z$, with a geometric embedding $i:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal T$ whose direct image is this inclusion. This is the closed subtopos complementary to $U$. For every Grothendieck topos $\mathcal E$, composition with $i$ identifies morphisms $\mathcal E\to\mathcal Z$ with morphisms $a:\mathcal E\to\mathcal T$ such that $a^{-1}U$ is initial, including their $2$-morphisms (natural transformations between direct-image functors as in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]). In particular, the inverse image of this closed subtopos under $a$ is the closed complement of $a^{-1}U$.

Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative ring and use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant ring sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Write $i^*$ for inverse image on these modules, with its adjunction $i^*\dashv i_*$. The functor $i_*$ on these modules is exact and fully faithful, its adjunction counit $i^*i_*\to1$ is an isomorphism, and its essential image consists exactly of modules $M$ with $j^*M=0$. Equivalently, for such $M$ the actual adjunction unit $M\to i_*i^*M$ is an isomorphism.

For any closed immersion of schemes $k:F\hookrightarrow S$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], its geometric morphism on small etale topoi [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] identifies $F_{\mathrm{Et}}$ with this closed complement in $S_{\mathrm{Et}}$ for the subterminal sheaf represented by $S\setminus F$.

The scheme example is etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04CA (proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward)(1). The factorization characterization is the universal-property form of the closed complement, recorded as an agent formulation of this construction.

proof.text: The construction of the complementary closed topos and its universal property is exactly [lem-trf-topos-complement-factorization]. Applying that statement with $\mathcal E=\mathcal T$ and $u=U$ gives the topos $\mathcal Z$, the geometric embedding $i$, and the identification of geometric morphisms $\mathcal E	o\mathcal Z$ with those $a:\mathcal E	o\mathcal T$ for which $a^{-1}U$ is initial. The cited universal property includes the corresponding 2-morphisms, so the factorization is unique up to unique compatible isomorphism. It also identifies the inverse image of the closed subtopos under any $a$ with the closed complement of $a^{-1}U$.

source.place: Tags 08LY, 08LZ and 08M0: construction and universal property of the closed complementary subtopos.

proof.text: The module assertion is obtained by applying the constant-ring module inverse-image/direct-image construction of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] to the closed embedding in [lem-trf-topos-complement-factorization]. Its direct image has the underlying sheaf-of-abelian-groups direct image, and its counit is an isomorphism because the underlying geometric embedding is fully faithful. A module $M$ satisfies $j^*M=0$ exactly when its underlying sheaf satisfies $U\times M\to U$ is an isomorphism, since the inverse-image comparison of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] forgets to the ordinary inverse image and the zero module has terminal underlying sheaf. Hence the underlying object of such an $M$ is in the essential image of the closed direct image. Choose an underlying preimage $N$ and an isomorphism $i_*N\cong M$. Full faithfulness descends the addition and zero maps of $M$ uniquely to $N$; the canonical constant-ring comparison descends the scalar action uniquely as well, and the module axioms descend because $i_*$ is faithful. Thus $N$ is a constant-$\Lambda$ module and $M\cong i_*N$, proving the supported essential-image characterization and the unit isomorphism for supported modules. For a short exact sequence in the closed module category, $i_*$ preserves kernels as a right adjoint. If $Q$ is the ambient cokernel of the resulting map, exactness of $j^*$ and $j^*i_*=0$ give $j^*Q=0$, so the characterization puts $Q$ in the essential image; applying exact $i^*$ and the counit identifies $i^*Q$ with the closed cokernel. Thus $i_*$ preserves cokernels and is exact.

source.place: Tag 08M3, lemma-i-star-equivalence, together with Tags 03DI, 0710 and 04EQ for the module adjunction and support description.

proof.text: Let $k:F\hookrightarrow S$ be a closed immersion and let $U=S\setminus F$. Apply the current statement of [lem-trf-etale-closed-complement-sets] to this closed immersion, on sheaves of sets and with the scheme-induced geometric-morphism adjunction specified there. Its direct image is fully faithful, its counit is invertible, and its essential image consists exactly of sheaves whose restriction to $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$ is terminal. For the subterminal sheaf $u$ represented by $U$, this last condition is precisely that $u\times H\to u$ is an isomorphism: open restriction is pullback to the slice over $u$, whose terminal object is $u\to u$. Thus this essential image is exactly the full subcategory defining the closed complement in [lem-trf-topos-complement-factorization]. Full faithfulness and equality of essential images give an equivalence over $S_{\mathrm{Et}}$ between $F_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and that closed complement, as claimed. This uses the set-valued assertion, with no passage from an abelian-sheaf result.

lean.note: Uses the existing closedComplementObjects and GeometricMorphism, normalized ConstantLeftModuleInverseImageLift, and actual etaleSetDirectImage.
